mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility, from -35.7% to -25.4%, indicates a strong underlying momentum for recovery in discretionary spending and out-of-home activities, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not show a mean increase compared to the last 28 days, or its upward trend reverses significantly.

mechanism_narrative: A substantial increase in WORKPLACES mobility, rising from -39.9% to -31.6% in the last week, suggests a policy-driven or employer-mandated return to offices, which will increase weekday foot traffic and drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility fails to sustain its recent increase or RETAIL_REC does not improve despite a continued rise in WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: The combined trend of decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility and increasing TRANSIT usage indicates a strong behavioral shift towards spending less time at home and more time commuting and engaging in out-of-home activities, directly boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases or TRANSIT mobility declines, or RETAIL_REC does not improve despite these trends.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility crossing above its baseline (from -0.7% to 2.1%) signifies a return to essential out-of-home errands and a general comfort with public spaces, which typically precedes or coincides with increased discretionary retail activity, driving RETAIL_REC up over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility falls back below baseline or RETAIL_REC does not show an improvement within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM crossing the baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent upward trend in TRANSIT mobility, despite still being significantly below baseline, indicates a gradual but steady return of public transport usage for various purposes, which will inevitably lead to increased footfall in retail areas and higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility stagnates or declines, or RETAIL_REC does not improve despite continued increases in TRANSIT usage.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp week-on-week decline in PARKS mobility from 7.3% to -28.3% suggests a seasonal shift away from outdoor leisure activities, potentially redirecting recreational spending and time towards indoor retail and entertainment options, leading to a short-term boost in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 20 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following a significant drop in PARKS mobility, or PARKS mobility recovers quickly.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous and significant increases in both WORKPLACES and GROCERY_PHARM mobility signal a broad resumption of daily routines involving commuting and essential errands, creating more opportunities for incidental and planned retail visits, thereby driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or GROCERY_PHARM mobility declines, or RETAIL_REC does not improve despite both showing upward trends.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility consistently declining and now falling below 15% above baseline (from 17.9% to 14.0%) indicates a sustained behavioral shift where people are spending significantly less time at home, directly translating to increased out-of-home activity and higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility reverses its downward trend and increases, or RETAIL_REC does not improve despite RESIDENTIAL remaining below the 15% threshold.
